versions.title: The Door That Was Not There
highlights: macOS is back. v0.14.3 was the first release in this game's history to ship no Mac build at all -- the export died on a Windows icon file the engine cannot decode, and reported nothing but a bare failure

When the patch notes do not appear, the game now tells you WHICH of five things went wrong, gives you a code you can quote, and offers a way to report it -- instead of one reassuring sentence that was only true in one of the five cases

added: A report affordance on the What's New screen, reachable with (R). It exists only when something is actually broken, so its absence is itself a statement that nothing is wrong.
changed: Every state of the What's New screen carries its own words, its own reference code, and its own consequence. A missing file, a corrupt file and a genuinely quiet release used to be indistinguishable (#1311).
fixed: The macOS build exports again. The macOS preset had been pointed at a .ico file, which the engine has no decoder for; it now uses the same PNG it used through v0.14.2 (#1305).

versions.title: Things That Charged You And Did Nothing
highlights: Compute engineers are people. An acquired startup's engineers used to show on the employee screen and never load into the sim -- they consumed stationery and produced nothing
The desperation lever stops quoting a doom figure it never applied. It now routes real safety absorption, so the button does what the text says
Your ad campaign reports itself every month, including the months nobody applies -- a barren month used to be silent and indistinguishable from no campaign at all
A rejected offer leaves a mark: the same lowball is no longer a guaranteed eventual hire, and the panel tells you so
Counter-offers keep a named person, raise their loyalty, and raise their salary forever -- an $80,000 option that previously did nothing
Send Feedback (N) now offers three one-click ways to actually send it. It used to save a file to your disk and ask you to email it

added: Counter-offers retain a named researcher, at a permanent payroll cost. Item 4 of the hiring-panel set; #1225 is still OPEN.
The onboarding bill and visa obligation are previewed before you commit. Item 5 of the hiring-panel set; #1225 is still OPEN.
Ad campaigns emit a monthly report whether or not anyone applied, and name what the campaign cost when it closes. Item 3 of the hiring-panel set; #1225 is still OPEN.
A signed-build path: tooling exists and is tested, awaiting the certificate. #1038 is still OPEN.
docs/TRUST.md, generated from source -- every point the game reaches outside its own process. #1038 is still OPEN.
changed: Compute engineers are real staff rather than an integer counter (#1247)
The header stops calling committed Attention 'queued', and hiring says days. #1223 is still OPEN.
The music conductor takes a nudge, and a pick made mid-crossfade is no longer dropped (#1249)
The game ships with its own icon instead of the default engine one -- visible in the taskbar, alt-tab, and the Windows publisher warning
fixed: The game-over screen stops blaming crises the player actually survived (#1248)
The desperation lever applies real safety absorption instead of a printed figure (#967)
An offer at or below a previously rejected figure is refused rather than silently accepted. Item 2 of the hiring-panel set; #1225 is still OPEN.

versions.title: The Game Stops Doing Things Silently
highlights: NEW BOARD. Ladder epoch L4 -> L5: the doom maths and the event deck both changed, so scores are not comparable with L4 runs. Your L4 scores stay valid and stay visible under L4
A doom sink that quietly drained up to -6 doom per turn is closed -- runtime events now route through the doom streams like everything else
28 new events, filling every risk-pool and severity combination, with varied numbers of options instead of the same three-option shape
Every response window now tells you the Attention it will charge, before you spend it
When the game refuses an action it now says so where you are looking, and says whether it is a rule or an unfinished feature
The month review is three times the size, typeset, and no longer covers the feed
One font-size setting now moves the whole game

added: 28 new events covering every risk pool and severity cell (#1230)
The cold-open arrival: a portal stitch and a held frame before the first screen (#1196)
Response windows advertise their Attention cost up front (#1217)
changed: The month review is a clipboard: about three times the area, typeset, and it no longer sits over the feed you were reading (#1231)
One font-size lever moves every unoverridden screen, and the guide stopped scrolling in five directions at once (#1236)
The first screen was rewritten to be legible to someone who has never played (#1205)
A refusal now states whether it is a rule or a stub, so 'you cannot do that' and 'this is not built yet' stop looking identical (#1222)
Monthly Attention capacity is derived in one place instead of several (#1211)
fixed: Runtime pdoom-data event options bypassed the doom streams entirely, acting as a sink of up to -6 doom per turn (#1233). THIS CHANGES RUN OUTCOMES and is why the ladder forks
PLAN-time rejections went to a hidden feed instead of to the player (#1204)
Submenu-driven refusals were invisible: the message existed and never reached a surface you were looking at (#1220)
The Operator name was collected at signup and then carried nowhere, and long names were being amputated rather than truncated (#1176)
12 live contact addresses were redacted from the bundled historical events (#1212)

versions.title: You Can See Your Own Board Again
highlights: Same board as v0.14.0 -- ladder L4, seed weekly-2026-w32. Your scores are still there and still count
The game-over screen no longer scrolls, and the Leaderboard is a button instead of a line you had to scroll to find
The leaderboard opens on the GLOBAL board instead of showing you only your own four scores
If your score did not go to the global board, the game now tells you why, every run
A successful submission is legible: bigger text, above the buttons instead of the last line on the screen
A failed upload names the actual fault instead of always saying 'offline'
In-game patch notes are back, and cover 0.12.0 onwards

added: Patch notes for 0.12.0 through 0.14.0 -- three releases where this screen had nothing to say
The release manifest publishes the league seed, so the website reads the board key instead of guessing it
changed: The leaderboard screen opens on the global board. Builds with no leaderboard configured are unchanged and stay local-only
The global fetch and the local view now read one board key from the board on screen, instead of two sources that could disagree
fixed: The game-over screen scrolled, and the only route to the leaderboard was the last line inside the scroll. It is a button now, the screen is shorter, and the body text is bigger
Two colours on the game-over screen failed accessible-contrast thresholds against the panel behind them

A player who never opted in, and a player who declined, both saw nothing at game over -- both are now told where the score went and where to change it. It is a readout, not a prompt, and it does not opt anybody in
The submit confirmation was small and below the buttons, so a successful upload looked like nothing happening

A rotated token, a moved endpoint and a server fault all reported 'offline'. The real status reaches you now, and offline means the request never reached a server. Either way your score is kept locally

versions.title: Ladder L4 -- The Comparability Fork
highlights: New ladder epoch L4 -- scores from this version are NOT comparable with the L3 board
Your L3 entries are still valid and still visible; they live on the L3 board
Featured league seed rolls to weekly-2026-w32
Pick the music from the pause menu, mid-run
A credits screen you can actually reach

added: Music track selection in the pause menu -- change the track while you play, not only in Settings
A credits screen, reachable from the main menu
Month review now shows what CHANGED since last month, and SPACE opens it
Settings rebuilt as a front card plus an operations board, so the common dials are on the first screen
A one-time 'claim a name' prompt before your first leaderboard upload, plus a lab-name generator
The update check now reads the release manifest and tells you when an update forks your board
changed: WHY THE BOARD FORKED: the historical event deck was retimed to one turn = one month, and the ruled event promotions were applied. Different events now fire on the same seed, so an L4 run is not comparable to an L3 run. That is the whole reason for the new epoch
Difficulty is now locked where the value is USED, not just on one screen, and using Alpha Tools sets a sticky unranked flag on the run
Keyboard navigation unified -- one table of choice keys, and one way out of every panel
The last player-facing 'AP' is gone, and numbers are formatted the same way everywhere
The player guide, the win condition and the cold open were rewritten to describe the game that actually exists
The turn-1 action hand fits above the fold, and Fundraising is the first tile
The debug event-trigger was deleted outright rather than hidden behind a guard
Contact addresses were redacted from the bundled historical events
The pause menu now grows to fit its text instead of growing its padding
fixed: The achievement toast rendered as a giant purple rectangle in 0.13.2
The office cat was a magenta checkerboard in every shipped build
The server rack painted over the event feed, and staff sprites were oversized
The public build wore a stale, clipped 'DEV BUILD' banner
A failed global leaderboard fetch is now VISIBLE instead of silent, and the SmartScreen warning is explained
Music was too loud and started on the wrong track; Graphics Settings was an empty header
Percent rounding ties are pinned, so doom reads the same number on every platform
The backslash dev key works again in release builds

versions.title: League Build -- Ladder L3
highlights: New ladder epoch L3 -- the effort economy was rebuilt, so scores are not comparable with L2 boards
A real first fifteen minutes: start in a bedroom, then choose your first office
Conference trips are a real commitment, not a menu skip
'Accept Your Fate' -- end a run on purpose and still reach the leaderboard

added: Early game: you start in a free bedroom or basement with a 2-hire cap, then pick one of three first offices -- a cheap-in cheap-out co-working corner, a balanced second-floor walk-up, or a bigger university annex sublet. Each has its own deposit, monthly rent, desk count, lease term and break fee, and the pick is locked in for now
Scouting actions for finding your next hire, including a deliberately loud strategic-shitposting option

Conference travel: the Travel submenu can send you to one of three conferences. Going costs real travel cash and drains your remaining Attention for the trip. The world keeps running while you are away, and you come home to a single 'while you were away' digest instead of a stack of missed-turn popups
'Accept Your Fate' lets you end a run deliberately and still post a score
Founder Attention replaces the per-turn AP pool, with four-way founder hours: doors, approvals, audits and reserve
Researcher quirks, with appetites that can be satisfied and a doom channel of their own
Four more office workers with idle, working and stressed mood art, and full walk cycles
A launch-time update check, so you find out a new build exists
changed: Difficulty is locked to Standard for league runs -- one comparable ladder while the player base is small
Scenario runs are UNRANKED, and you are told so before you pick one
The leaderboard screen now explains what a board IS, on the screen where people look at boards
Player-facing 'AP' retired from the UI
fixed: Hire candidates could silently vanish: if your cash dropped between queuing a hire and it executing later the same turn, the candidate left the pool but was never hired, with no message. Stranded hires now return to the pool, and existing saves self-heal

Publishing papers and safety research were wired to zero doom effect since the doom-engine migration -- they read as working but did nothing. They are priced now and actually fire, along with safety audits and the lobbying, rival and open-source doom streams
Six upgrades that did nothing were either wired up or removed
Dialogs now stack properly, so an event opening over another dialog can no longer strand it
Several ways to kill a run on re-entry -- starting a new game over a running one, returning from the dev overlay, and Play Again
Four presentation bugs found in the league-build playtest

versions.title: Soft-Lock Hotfixes
highlights: Two bugs that could strand a session are fixed
No other gameplay changes -- this is a hotfix on the L2 board, not a new epoch

changed: Three hiring and travel buttons that promised more than they delivered were right-sized
fixed: An event opening over the ledger orphaned the ledger dialog, leaving it un-closeable and the session stuck
Closing a staff card with ESC could leave an input blocker alive, deadening the mouse for the rest of the session

versions.title: Ladder L2 -- Epoch Cut
highlights: New ladder epoch L2 -- scores are not comparable with L1 boards
A diegetic cold open: a phone, a passcode, and a hold-to-skip
Choose non-profit or for-profit in the early game
Costs are on the button face, not hidden behind a hover

added: Onboarding cold open -- a phone-and-passcode intro you can hold a key to skip, with a setting to turn intros off
A non-profit versus for-profit choice in the early game, with its own funding seeds
A rotating featured league seed
Staged dossier portraits on candidate and employee cards
changed: Action costs are shown on the button face instead of hover-only
The ledger shows debt due-dates as calendar dates, not turn counts
The settings menu scrolls when its content overflows the screen
Music starts quieter
fixed: The event dialog stays OPEN when you pick a choice you cannot afford, instead of closing on you
An unaffordable event window now lapses cleanly instead of orphaning the dialog and locking the session
A window option resolved against the wrong event when several were queued
Overbooking your turn no longer leaves phantom tiles in the queue, and can no longer soft-lock the turn
The leaderboard crash on opening the board from a key press

versions.title: Attention, the Ledger, and the Doom Engine
highlights: Attention replaces per-turn AP -- a monthly founder budget you spend where it matters
The Liability Ledger: the debts and exposures you accumulate are now a screen you can read
Doom is nine accumulating streams with a colour-coded blow-by-blow, not a mystery number
Rival labs act visibly, and the defeat screen tells you who killed you
Global leaderboards are live

added: Attention economy: a monthly founder budget replaces the per-turn AP pool
The Liability Ledger -- a player-facing screen for the obligations and exposures you take on, with a compact summary and a keybind to open it
Cost-of-debt pricing and financing instruments, so borrowing has a real price
Doom as nine accumulating streams, with a colour-coded per-source breakdown you can read turn by turn
Rival labs act in the feed (filterable), appear in the month review, and are revealed as you discover them
Death attribution: the defeat screen reports the real cause, including which rival contributed
A hiring pipeline -- source, interview, offer, onboard -- with candidate cards carrying hidden appetites and quirks that reveal as you learn about them
Research quality: a Rushed / Standard / Thorough toggle that trades speed against risk, feeding the hidden risk pool
Scenario and mod hooks: drop a JSON file into the scenarios folder to add a scenario, with three samples included
Save and load with a full-state round trip
An office floor you can watch -- walkers mirror your staff count, with directional walk cycles
An adaptive score that follows the doom band
A first-launch welcome overlay, with a hints toggle
Global leaderboards went live, with a remote score-sync client
Runs are deterministic from a seed and can be replayed from a canonical input string, which is what makes a shared board mean anything
changed: Turns-survived is the primary score, compared lexicographically
The doom <= 0 instant victory was removed -- there is no winning by driving the number to zero
Difficulty is selectable in the UI and its modifiers are actually applied
Salary cadence made sustainable, with a bankruptcy warning before it bites
Committing a turn always advances, and there is a share line for your result
Global keybinds now yield to focused text fields and dialogs
fixed: Compute is actually consumed by research and actions
Hiring works for all researcher specializations, not just some
Rival labs contribute scaling doom pressure instead of sitting inert
No event fires before your first turn, and the number of events per turn is capped
The ledger no longer dead-ends, and ESC and back behave consistently across screens
Event outcomes that read as mechanical but did nothing were audited and fixed or removed
The paper-decision flood was throttled and event dialog text wraps
Game over no longer quits to the desktop
Opening the leaderboard is faster and no longer loads the whole population into memory

versions.title: Travel & Conferences System
highlights: What's New Modal - See patch notes on first launch after updates
Academic Conference System - Submit papers to NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, and more
Travel Cost System - Realistic flight and accommodation costs
Jet Lag Mechanics - Travel class affects researcher productivity

added: What's New modal showing patch notes on first launch after updates
What's New button in main menu to view patch notes anytime
Academic Conference System with 9 real-world AI conferences
Travel submenu with paper submission and conference attendance
Paper review process with multi-turn decision cycles
Three travel classes: Economy, Business, First Class
Jet lag affecting researcher productivity based on travel class
Public opinion meter affecting fundraising and events
Responsive UI layout adapting to screen sizes
fixed: AP Double-Spend Bug - Actions no longer deduct AP twice
Poaching Event Infinite Loop - Now respects probability
Manager Threshold - First 9 researchers now founder-managed
Hiring Queue - Support for multiple hires per turn
Event Popup AP Display - Shows correct available AP

versions.title: Playtesting Fixes & Turn Philosophy
highlights: Bug Reporter Integration - In-game bug reporting with backslash or N key
Turn Philosophy Reframe - 'Monday Planning' metaphor
Event Dialog UX Improvements - Better visibility and interaction

added: In-game bug reporting system (backslash or N)
Cat contributor recognition system
Comprehensive turn sequence documentation
fixed: Turn advancement with empty action queue now works
Event AP Logic uses available AP correctly
Employee screen display renders correctly
changed: Turn Philosophy: 'Skip Turn' renamed to 'Commit Plan & Reserve AP'
Event dialog background improved for visibility

versions.title: Multi-Platform Release & Enhanced CI/CD
highlights: Multi-Platform Build Support - Windows, Linux, and macOS
Enhanced CI/CD Pipeline - Automated validation and releases
Employee Management Screen - Tab-based interface

added: Automated builds for Windows, Linux, and macOS
Linux/X11 and macOS export presets
Release metadata generation (JSON + RSS feeds)
Employee Management Screen with progressive warnings
